title: Three-marginal Coulomb transport
author: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic)
description: OpenAI's counterexample (2026) to the Monge ansatz for three particles: for every dimension d >= 2 and every Riesz exponent s > 0, in particular for the Coulomb cost in three dimensions, there is a smooth compactly supported density with smooth square root for which the three-marginal transport minimum is finite and attained, but by no pair of measure-preserving maps, although such maps come arbitrarily close. The first lesson proves the two abstract steps: a supporting potential confines optimal couplings to a contact set, and a mass imbalance forbids every selection among four branches. The second builds the potential by local calculus near two collinear triples sharing a central point. The third shows that the Monge and Kantorovich values agree, with Rosenblatt's transform between absolutely continuous measures. The fourth restates nonattainment and the approximation with Robinson's infinitesimals, built from an ultrafilter: an internal pair of maps at an infinitely fine resolution exceeds the minimum by a positive infinitesimal, and its standard part is the optimal coupling, which is not given by maps.
